title: Joining Sophie's Squad to Support Mental Wellness - NewsBreak
text:
By Full Range Media October 2, 2026 ,
7 hours ago
The Hibbing/Chisholm Bluejackets and the Grand Rapids Thunderhawks were fierce competitors on the field Thursday afternoon, but before the start of Thursday’s contest, the two girls soccer teams combined for an even more important goal.
The players teamed up for Sophie’s Squad, A nonprofit organization dedicated to improving the mental health of youth and college athletes by raising awareness, removing the stigma associated with seeking help, and fostering open conversation.
It was founded in 2021 by Terry Hughes, a youth hockey coach, in honor of Sophie Wieland, a 14-year-old hockey player who died by suicide. Its mission is to combat the intense pressures athletes face, normalize mental health struggles, and emphasize that asking for help is a sign of strength.
The group provides athletes, parents, and coaches with accessible mental health tools, resources, and reminders that they do not have to struggle alone.
Thursday’s program was hosted by mental health professional Jeff Laitala and Lori Laitala, who lost her son to suicide, and consisted of a talk with both teams expressing mental health care, a ceremonial first kick, an information booth with resource materials, and messages over the loudspeaker throughout the game.
Jeff McNickle is a mental health professional and chaplain with the St. Louis County Sheriff’s Department who often responds to suicide calls.
McNickle said that he worked with Sophie’s Squad in the past and wanted to bring it to Hibbing High School this year. He spoke with the Hibbing/Chisholm Head Coach, Brittany Lindstrom, who was immediately on board with the program; he made a quick call to Grand Rapids coach Brooke Moses, and the Thunderhawks and Bluejackets were a team in support of mental health.
If you would like more information about Sophie’s Squad, it can be found at http://www.sophiessquad.org, and if you are suffering from a mental health crisis, help can be found with the suicide & Crisis Lifeline by text, call, or chat at 988.
Once the game started, the partners in mental health care once again became competitors, with Grand Rapids coming out ahead in the game with an offensive display of power, resulting in a 9-0 Grand Rapids victory.
summary: The players teamed up for Sophie’s Squad, A nonprofit organization dedicated to improving the mental health of youth and college athletes by raising awareness, removing the stigma associated with seeking help, and fostering open conversation. Its mission is to combat the intense pressures athletes face, normalize mental health struggles, and emphasize that asking for help is a sign of strength.
